  • Try downloading from different device

  • Disable browser extensions temporarily
  • Use a different browser
  • Clear browser cache completely

What is SSC City Intimation Slip 2026?

The SSC City Intimation Slip 2026 is an advance notification document released before the admit card. It provides candidates with essential preliminary information about their examination to help them make necessary travel and accommodation arrangements. The city slip is NOT your admit card but serves as an important reference document.

Key Information Available in City Slip:

  • Allotted exam city and state
  • Scheduled exam date
  • Shift timing (Morning/Afternoon/Evening)
  • Reporting time at exam center
  • Gate closing time
  • Candidate's name and registration number
  • Category (SC/ST/OBC/General/EWS)
  • PwBD status (if applicable)

Important Notice: The city intimation slip is NOT your admit card and does not permit you to appear in the exam. It is only for informational purposes. You must download the admit card separately (available from 15th January 2026) to enter the examination hall.

How to Download SSC City Intimation Slip 2026? (Step-by-Step Guide)

Step 1: Visit Official Website

  • Open your web browser (Chrome, Firefox, or Edge recommended)
  • Visit SSC official website: ssc.gov.in
  • Or use your regional SSC portal if applicable
  • Ensure you have stable internet connection
  • On the homepage, scroll down to "Latest Updates" or "Important Links" section
  • Look for link: "SSC CGL Tier 2 City Intimation Slip 2026" or "Check City Intimation for SSC CGL 2025 (Tier-II)"
  • Click on the city intimation slip download link
  • You may be redirected to a candidate login page
  • Enter your Registration Number (or Username/OTR)
  • Enter your Password (or Date of Birth if applicable)
  • Type the Captcha Code as shown in the image (case-sensitive)
  • Double-check all entered information for accuracy
  • Click on the "Submit" or "Login" button
  • Your city intimation slip will appear on the screen
  • Carefully verify all details displayed
  • Check: Name, Registration No., Exam City, Date, Shift Timing
  • Click on "Download" or "Save as PDF" button
  • Save the file to your computer/mobile device
  • Take a printout of the city slip for reference
  • Save a backup copy in cloud storage (Google Drive/Email)
  • Keep both digital and physical copies safe

Download your city intimation slip as soon as it is released to avoid server overload and last-minute technical issues. The website may experience heavy traffic during peak hours.

Common Issues & Solutions While Downloading City Slip

Issue #1: Unable to Login / Invalid Credentials Error

Solutions:

  • Verify your registration number carefully (no spaces before/after)
  • Check password (case-sensitive) or reset if forgotten
  • Ensure CAPS LOCK is off while entering details
  • Clear your browser cache and cookies (Ctrl+Shift+Del)
  • Try using a different web browser (Chrome, Firefox, or Edge)
  • Use "Forgot Password" link if needed
  • Check your registered email for confirmation

Issue #2: City Slip Not Showing / Page Not Loading

Solutions:

  • Verify if city slip is released for your specific exam date
  • Try downloading during non-peak hours (early morning 6-8 AM or late night 11 PM onwards)
  • Disable VPN, proxy, or ad-blocker extensions
  • Check your internet connection stability
  • Try using mobile data instead of WiFi (or vice versa)
  • Use incognito/private browsing mode
  • Update your web browser to the latest version

Issue #3: Error in Details Displayed on City Slip

Solutions:

  • Contact SSC helpdesk immediately
  • Email to: helpdesk email available on ssc.gov.in with screenshot
  • Call helpline: Check official website for contact (working hours)
  • Keep your registration number and application details ready
  • Explain the exact discrepancy in detail
  • Request for correction before exam date

Issue #4: PDF Download Not Working

Solutions:

  • Take a screenshot of the city slip as backup
  • Try "Print to PDF" option (Ctrl+P then save as PDF)
  • Use a different PDF reader (Adobe Acrobat Reader)
  • Check if pop-ups are blocked in browser settings
  • Ensure sufficient storage space on device
  • Try downloading from different device

Issue #5: Captcha Not Visible or Loading

Solutions:

  • Refresh the page (F5 key)
  • Enable JavaScript in browser settings
  • Disable browser extensions temporarily
  • Use a different browser
  • Clear browser cache completely

City Intimation Slip vs Admit Card - Key Differences

Many candidates confuse city intimation slip with admit card. Here's a clear comparison to understand the differences:

Aspect City Intimation Slip Admit Card / Hall Ticket
Purpose Advance information only for travel planning Mandatory entry document for examination
Release Time 7-10 days before exam date 2-3 days before exam date
Information Provided Exam city, date, shift timing only Complete center address, roll number, photo, signature
Can you enter exam hall? ❌ NO - Not permitted ✅ YES - Mandatory requirement
Contains Photo ❌ No ✅ Yes
Contains Roll Number ❌ No ✅ Yes
Exam Center Address Only city name Complete address with venue details
Use for Travel Booking ✅ Yes - Use for advance planning Can use after release
Barcode/QR Code Usually not present Present for verification
Exam Instructions General instructions Detailed exam day instructions

Critical Warning: You CANNOT enter the examination hall with only the city intimation slip. You MUST download and carry the admit card (available from 15th January 2026) along with a valid photo ID proof to appear for the exam.

Download your SSC CGL Tier 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 immediately from ssc.gov.in and start planning your travel! All the best for your exam!

SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Selection for engagement of apprentices will be based on (i) Online Written Test and (ii) Test of Local Language, followed by Medical Examination. Final selection is subject to verification of eligibility, qualifying in local language test, and medical fitness. A Wait List (State-category wise) will be maintained for one year from the date of result or next engagement exercise, whichever is earlier. Candidates will be released only once from this waitlist against non-joining subject to availability of qualified candidates.

SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 - Weightage in Junior Associate Recruitment

Weightage/Relaxation to apprentices in recruitment of Junior Associates shall be given as per the recruitment policy of the Bank as amended from time to time, to apprentices who successfully complete the apprenticeship training in SBI, subject to candidate's satisfactory conduct and performance during the entire training period. Successful completion refers to passing of the skill evaluation test (Trade test) and obtention of the joint National Apprenticeship Certificate issued by SBI-NSDC / BFSI-SSC.

Competition Level Analysis for SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026

The competition level for SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 is expected to be very high due to 7150 seats being offered at the all-India level and the exam being open to any graduate, including those already preparing for bank and SSC exams. While the written test is of easy to moderate difficulty and slightly below SBI Clerk level, the large number of serious aspirants in high-population states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana will push state-wise and category-wise cut-offs upward.

In practical terms, each seat is likely to attract dozens to over a hundred candidates in major states, making speed, accuracy, and sectional balance crucial to clearing the single-stage written exam followed by the local language test. However, the effective competition reduces at later stages because some candidates will fail to qualify the language test or be filtered out at the document verification, CIBIL, Aadhaar, and medical fitness stages, and SBI will finally select candidates strictly on state-wise and category-wise merit from those who clear all stages.

Who should NOT apply for SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026?

  • Candidates looking for a permanent job in SBI; this is only a 1‑year apprenticeship with no guarantee of absorption or regular employment.
  • Candidates who already completed any Apprenticeship (in SBI or any other organisation) or are currently undergoing apprenticeship training under the Apprentices Act.
  • Candidates outside the age band 20–28 years as on the cut-off date (even 1 day younger/older is not eligible, except notified relaxations for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD).
  • Aspirants who do not have a Graduation degree from a recognised University/Institute by the specified date.
  • Candidates not fluent in the notified local language of the State/UT (reading, writing, speaking, understanding), and who are unlikely to clear the language test or do not have 10th/12th proof.
  • Candidates unwilling or unable to register on the NAPS portal before applying, as this is a mandatory prerequisite for SBI Apprentice.
  • Candidates with serious CIBIL/loan/credit‑card defaults who have not regularised or repaid outstanding dues by the time of offer; such profiles are normally rejected in bank recruitments.
  • Ex‑Servicemen / Disabled Ex‑Servicemen, where the notification clearly states no engagement / no reservation for them under Apprentice.
  • PwBD candidates whose disability type falls under “likely to improve” (temporary disability) where reservation benefits may not apply as per notification conditions.
  • Candidates who cannot produce valid Aadhaar (except where exempted, e.g., certain North‑Eastern states with alternate ID allowed).

Common mistakes / What to check before applying SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026?

  • Applying in a wrong State or language where you cannot comfortably read, write and speak the specified local language.
  • Entering wrong category (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/UR); category cannot be changed later and mismatch with certificates at DV can lead to cancellation.
  • OBC candidates from creamy layer applying as OBC instead of UR; only non‑creamy OBCs with valid, recent certificate get reservation.
  • Uploading blurred/incorrect photo, signature, thumb impression or declaration (wrong size, wrong format, someone else’s handwriting) leading to rejection at scrutiny.
  • Using invalid or inactive mobile number/email ID, causing failure to receive OTPs, registration details, call letters or further communication.
  • Submitting multiple applications for different states or with different details; SBI usually accepts only the last complete application and may forfeit extra fees.
  • Ignoring negative marking and over‑attempting in the exam, which can sharply reduce your score despite high attempts.
  • Not reading the clause that this is not regular employment, and later protesting about absorption or permanent posting after apprenticeship ends.

How to Apply for SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Candidates shall apply online; no other mode of application will be accepted. Candidates must first mandatorily register on the NAPS portal (https://apprenticeshipindia.gov.in) and read the detailed guidelines on https://bfsissc.com before applying online through the SBI website.

Candidates should have a valid email ID and mobile number which should be kept active till declaration of results. Candidates are advised to apply well before the closing date and not wait till the last date.

Documents Required to be Scanned and Uploaded (as per Annexure-I):

  • Recent passport-size colour photograph (4.5 cm × 3.5 cm; 200×230 pixels; 20 KB–50 KB; JPEG)
  • Signature with black ink on white paper (140×60 pixels; 10 KB–20 KB; JPEG)
  • Left Thumb Impression on white paper with black or blue ink (240×240 pixels; 20 KB–50 KB; JPEG/JPG)

Documents to be Produced at the time of Examination / Document Verification / Engagement:

  • Caste Certificate in prescribed Government of India format (for SC/ST candidates) — to be submitted at the time of engagement if called for
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate in prescribed Government of India format, issued during the period 01-04-2026 to the date of joining (for OBC candidates)
  • Income and Asset Certificate issued by Competent Authority in the format prescribed by Government of India, valid for the year 2026-27 (for EWS candidates)
  • Disability Certificate in prescribed format issued by a Competent Authority as per Government of India guidelines (for PwBD candidates)

Printout of Application Form is NOT to be sent to SBI. No Hard Copy of the Call Letter for Online Written Examination will be sent by post. Candidates must appear for the test at their own cost; SBI will not pay or reimburse any such expenses.

Apply Online at: https://www.sbi.co.in/careers or https://sbi.bank.in/careers

For queries: Call 022-22820427 (11:00 AM to 06:00 PM on working days) or visit https://cgrs.ibps.in — mention "Engagement of Apprentice in SBI" in the subject.

Important Instructions for SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 Candidates

  • THIS IS NOT AN EMPLOYMENT IN THE BANK. NOR IS THE SAME CONTRACT EMPLOYMENT. Candidates engaged as Apprentice will NOT be treated as "employees" of SBI and will not be entitled to receive any benefits available for employees of the Bank.
  • SBI shall have no obligation to offer regular employment to Apprentices during and/or after the completion of the Apprenticeship period. After completion, candidates will be relieved from the respective work area.
  • Candidates can apply for engagement in one State only and can appear for the examination only once under this engagement project.
  • Mandatory registration on NAPS portal (https://apprenticeshipindia.gov.in) before applying online on SBI website is required.
  • No Ex-Servicemen / Disabled Ex-Servicemen shall be engaged as an Apprentice and there is no reservation for Ex-Servicemen in the Apprentice Engagement.
  • OBC candidates belonging to the "Creamy Layer" are not entitled to reservation/relaxation; they should apply as General or General (LD/VI/HI/d&e) as applicable.

  • Candidates with CIBIL default record (unpaid loans/credit card dues) are not eligible for engagement until dues are regularized/repaid.
  • All candidates (except Northeastern State candidates) must produce Aadhaar Number before engagement/contract signing.
  • Not more than one application should be submitted; in case of multiple applications, only the last valid completed application will be retained and fee paid for other registrations will stand forfeited.
  • PwBD candidates with disability conditions falling under "likely to improve" (temporary disability) category are not eligible for reservation.

Scribe must be arranged by the candidate at his/her own cost. Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination is allowed (whether availing scribe or not) for eligible PwBD candidates.
  • Candidates are advised to keep their registered email ID/mobile active for receiving call letters/advices etc.

  • All revisions/corrigendum (if any) will be hosted on the Bank's website only — candidates should visit regularly.
  • No request for change of examination centre shall be entertained. No Travel Expenses will be reimbursed/paid by SBI.
  • Canvassing in any form will be a disqualification.
  • Legal jurisdiction for any dispute arising out of this recruitment shall be Mumbai only.
  • Bank reserves right to cancel the selection process partly/entirely at any stage.

Who Can Apply for RRB Technician 2026?

Eligibility criteria depend on the post and level. Candidates must meet educational, technical, and age requirements as per the Centralised Employment Notification.

  • Technician Grade I Signal: B.Sc. (Physics / Electronics / Computer Science / IT / Instrumentation) or Degree/Diploma in Engineering in relevant discipline from a recognized institution.
  • Technician Grade III: 10th / Matriculation plus ITI from NCVT/SCVT in relevant trade or Act Apprenticeship in the concerned trade.
  • Other Conditions: Candidates must satisfy prescribed medical standards and citizenship norms and should be within the specified age limit as on the date mentioned in CEN 02/2026.

Age Limit

  • Technician Grade I Signal: 18 to 36 Years
  • Technician Grade III: 18 to 33 Years
  • Upper age relaxation for reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC/NCL/EWS/Ex-Servicemen/ PWBD) will be applicable as per Government of India rules and details will be given in the detailed CEN. 

Selection Process

RRB Technician recruitment involves multiple stages including a Computer Based Test and subsequent document and medical verification. There is no Computer Based Aptitude Test for these Technician posts.

  • Stage 1: Computer Based Test (CBT)
  • Stage 2: Document Verification
  • Stage 3: Medical Examination

RRB Technician Exam Pattern 2026

  • Mode of Exam: Computer Based Test (CBT)
  • Total Questions: 100 Objective Type Questions
  • Total Marks: 100 Marks
  • Exam Duration: 90 Minutes
  • Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark will be deducted for each wrong answer; no negative marks for unattempted questions. 

Salary Details

  • Technician Grade I Signal: Pay Level 5 (7th CPC) – Initial Pay Rs. 29,200/-
  • Technician Grade III: Pay Level 2 (7th CPC) – Initial Pay Rs. 19,900/-
  • Additional allowances such as DA, HRA, TA and other benefits will be admissible as per Railway rules for the respective pay levels. 

How to Apply for RRB Technician Recruitment 2026

  • Visit your regional RRB website (e.g., Ahmedabad, Ajmer, Bengaluru, Chennai, Secunderabad, etc.).
  • Open the link for Centralised Employment Notification CEN 02/2026 – Technician.
  • Read the detailed notification carefully including post-wise eligibility, instructions and list of RRBs.
  • Register by providing basic details like name, mobile number and email ID.
  • Login using the registration credentials and fill the online application form for the desired post and pay level (only one RRB and one pay level allowed per candidate).
  • Upload required documents, photograph and signature as per specifications. >Pay the prescribed application fee through online mode, if applicable.
  • Submit the application form and take a printout / save PDF for future reference.

Important Points Mentioned in Indicative Notice

  • Each candidate can apply to only one RRB for a specific pay level and only one common online application is allowed for all notified posts in that pay level.
  • Separate applications must be submitted for each pay level, if eligible.
  • Candidates are strongly advised to verify name, date of birth and other details using Aadhaar to avoid mismatches at later stages.
  • RRBs caution candidates to be aware of touts, brokers and job racketeers and to rely only on official RRB websites for genuine information.

SSC CGL 2026 – Selection Process

Selection is through a two-tier Computer Based Examination (CBE). Marks scored in CBE conducted in multiple shifts will be normalized as per the procedure published by SSC vide Notice dated 02-06-2025. There is no provision for re-evaluation/re-checking of scores at any stage.

Tier-I consists of Objective Type / MCQ questions, set in English and Hindi (except English Comprehension). Negative marking: 0.50 marks per wrong answer.

Tier-II: Computer Based Examination

Tier-II is conducted in Paper-I, Paper-II, and Paper-III in separate shifts/days.

Negative marking in Tier-II: 1 mark per wrong answer in Section-I, II, III of Paper-I; 0.50 marks in Paper-II and Paper-III. Section-III (CKT) and Section-IV (DEST) are qualifying in nature. Candidates must qualify all sections of Paper-I separately. Higher standards of CKT and DEST are set for specific posts (CSS, MEA, AFHQ, SFIO, CBIC, Postal etc.). Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available for PwBD candidates eligible for scribe.

Tier-I: General Awareness Current events, India and neighbouring countries, History, Culture, Geography, Economic Scene, General Policy, Scientific Research
Tier-I: Quantitative Aptitude Whole numbers, decimals, fractions, percentages, ratio, averages, SI/CI, profit & loss, discount, time & work, time & distance, algebra, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, bar charts, pie charts
Tier-I: English Comprehension Grammar, vocabulary, comprehension, writing ability
Tier-II Paper-I Sec-I: Mathematical Abilities Number systems, arithmetic, algebra, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, statistics & probability
Tier-II Paper-I Sec-II: English Language & Comprehension Vocabulary, grammar, synonyms, antonyms, idioms, sentence improvement, comprehension passages (current affairs + editorial based)
Tier-II Paper-I Sec-III: Computer Knowledge Computer basics, MS Office (Word/Excel/PowerPoint), Internet & e-mail, networking & cybersecurity basics
Tier-II Paper-II: Statistics Data collection, frequency distribution, central tendency, dispersion, correlation, regression, probability, sampling theory, statistical inference, ANOVA, time series, index numbers
Tier-II Paper-III: General Studies (Finance & Economics) Part A (Finance & Accounts, 80 marks): Financial accounting, GAAP, books of accounts, depreciation, bank reconciliation. Part B (Economics & Governance, 120 marks): Economic concepts, Indian economy, governance, financial markets, budget basics

Competition Level Analysis for SSC CGL 2026

The overall competition level for SSC CGL 2026 is expected to remain very high because the examination attracts a massive number of graduate applicants every year across India. Even with around 12,256 vacancies, the effective competition ratio remains extremely tough for high-demand posts.

  1. Applicant volume is huge: SSC CGL is among the most sought-after central government exams, and premium posts receive intense preference from top scorers.
  2. Tier-I acts as the main screening stage: With negative marking and sectional timing, both speed and accuracy matter. Candidates targeting top posts generally need a very strong Tier-I score.
  3. Tier-II gets post-specific: Specialized posts like JSO and AAO attract a smaller but more qualified pool, making domain preparation more important than raw competition numbers.
  4. DEST and CKT can eliminate candidates: Although qualifying in nature, poor performance in these sections can disqualify otherwise strong candidates for certain posts.
  5. Physical standards create an extra filter: Certain Inspector and Sub Inspector posts require physical and medical fitness standards that are checked separately by user departments.

Who Should NOT Apply for SSC CGL 2026?

  1. Candidates who will not possess a Bachelor's Degree by 01-08-2026.
  2. Candidates who fall outside the age limit for all eligible posts even after applicable relaxation.
  3. OBC Creamy Layer candidates intending to claim OBC reservation.
  4. Candidates who cannot meet post-specific physical or medical standards for the posts they plan to prefer.
  5. Non-matriculate Ex-Servicemen or those who have not completed the required length of service.
  6. Candidates applying for JSO without the required Mathematics or Statistics qualification.
  7. Female candidates applying specifically for BRO vacancies, where only male candidates are eligible.
  8. Distance-learning degree holders without valid UGC-DEB approval for the relevant period.

Common Mistakes / What to Check Before Applying SSC CGL 2026

  1. Not generating a fresh OTR on the new SSC website.
  2. Using a pre-existing photograph instead of live photo capture where required.
  3. Uploading blurred or wrongly sized signature files.
  4. Selecting the wrong reservation category without valid supporting certificate.
  5. Ignoring post-specific standards before locking post preferences.
  6. Choosing JSO or AAO related preferences without being ready for Paper-II or Paper-III.
  7. Skipping Aadhaar-based authentication even when eligible.
  8. Waiting until the final date for application submission.
  9. Missing the answer key objection window after examination.
  10. Confusing the correction window fee structure.

How to Apply for SSC CGL 2026

Candidates must apply online only at https://ssc.gov.in or through the mY SSC mobile application (available on Store). No other mode of application is accepted. Candidates who have not generated OTR on the new website must do so first. Once OTR is generated on the new website, it remains valid for all future examinations on that portal.

Candidates are advised to opt for Aadhaar-based authentication during OTR. Aadhaar-authenticated candidates get significant exemptions: their applications are not rejected for photograph/signature standards, and they need not carry photo ID at the examination venue.

Steps to Apply:

  1. Generate One-Time Registration (OTR) at https://ssc.gov.in (mandatory; use Aadhaar-based authentication if possible)
  2. Complete OTR profile and lock it
  3. Fill the Common Application Form (CAF) including live photograph capture via camera
  4. Upload scanned signature (JPEG/JPG, 10–20 KB, 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm)
  5. Fill the Examination Specific Module (post preferences, exam centre choices - 3 centres within same region in order of priority)
  6. Pay application fee of Rs. 100/- online (if applicable) by 23-06-2026
  7. Preview/Print the application to verify all details before final submission
  8. Use the correction window (29-06 to 01-07-2026) if any correction is needed (chargeable)
  9. Keep printout of application and all documents for at least 3 years

Documents to Keep Ready for Document Verification (after final selection):

  • Matriculation/Secondary School Certificate (proof of date of birth)
  • Mark sheets for all years/semesters of Graduation + Provisional/Degree Certificate
  • SC/ST Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure of the notification)
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure-X); must be valid as on closing date of application
  • EWS Income & Asset Certificate valid for FY 2026–27 (issued based on income for FY 2025–26) in prescribed format (Annexure-XI)
  • PwBD Disability Certificate from competent authority specifying type of disability (as per Annexure-XII to XIII)
  • Ex-Serviceman discharge certificate and other relevant ESM documents
  • Equivalence certificate (for equivalent qualifications other than standard degrees)
  • DEB/UGC approval letter (for Distance Learning degree holders)
  • Certificate of proficiency in State Regional/official language (for AAO/Assistant Audit Officer State Cadre)

Apply Online at: https://ssc.gov.in | Toll Free Helpline: 1800 309 3063

Important Instructions for SSC CGL 2026 Candidates

  • Final allotment is based on merit-cum-preference, and no alternate post will be offered if a candidate fails post-specific standards after allotment.
  • OBC candidates claiming reservation must not belong to the creamy layer as on the closing date of application.
  • EWS certificate must be valid for FY 2026–27 and should be based on income for FY 2025–26.
  • PwBD candidates must choose the correct sub-category in the application form because no later change is allowed.
  • Scribe rules are strict: the scribe must complete OTR, be Aadhaar-authenticated, and cannot assist more than one candidate.
  • Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available to eligible PwBD candidates.
  • Tentative answer keys can be challenged online by paying Rs. 100 per question within the specified period only.
  • No re-evaluation or re-checking of scores is available at any stage.
  • Candidates should preserve the application form and related documents for at least 3 years.
  • Candidature remains provisional until certificates and documents are verified by the Appointing Authority.
  • Fraudulent claims of reservation status may lead to debarment from all SSC examinations.
  • Any update in exam schedule or process will be communicated through the SSC website only.
  • Applications without the required fee, unless exempted, or incomplete applications will be summarily rejected.

  • Only unmarried Indian male candidates are eligible. Agniveers cannot marry during their entire 4-year tenure; violation will result in dismissal from service.
  • Agniveers are enrolled under the Navy Act 1957 for a period of 4 years. Indian Navy is not obliged to retain Agniveers beyond the engagement period.
  • Up to 25% of each specific batch of Agniveers may be offered permanent enrolment in the Indian Navy as Sailors (Regular Cadre) / Artificers based on performance and organisational requirements. Selection for further enrolment is entirely at the discretion of the Indian Navy; Agniveers have no right to be selected.
  • Agniveers will not be permitted to seek release at their own request prior to completion of the engagement period.
  • Agniveers are not governed by Naval Pension Regulations/Rules and are not entitled to gratuity for the engagement period.
  • Agniveers will not be eligible for Ex-Servicemen status.
  • Candidates declaring incorrect domicile/gender and other details shall not be permitted to appear in the recruitment and their candidature will be cancelled.
  • Candidates reporting 30 minutes after the reporting time for Stage I - INET shall not be allowed to appear in the examination.
  • A candidate's selection pertaining to a particular batch is valid for that batch only. Qualified candidates whose names do not appear in the merit list cannot claim admission for the next batch.
  • Mobile phones or any other communication devices are not allowed inside the examination premises. Infringement will entail disciplinary action including ban from future examinations.
  • Candidates should not submit multiple applications. If more than one application is received, candidature will be cancelled.
  • Minimum height standard is 157 cms. Permanent body tattoos are only permitted on the inner face of forearms (inside of elbow to wrist) and on the reversed side of palm/back (dorsal) side of hand. Tattoos on any other part of the body are not acceptable.
  • Candidates are advised to get their ears cleaned for wax and tartar removed from teeth prior to medical examination.
  • Visual Standards: Uncorrected Vision 6/12, 6/12 | Corrected Vision 6/6, 6/6 | Colour Perception: CP PASS.
  • No enquiry will be entertained regarding this recruitment/enrolment after a period of six months post completion of the recruitment cycle for the respective batch.
  • The terms and conditions given in the advertisement are guidelines only and are subject to change without notice. Further, orders issued by the Government as amended from time to time will apply for selected candidates.

BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Selection will be based on Computer Based Multiple Choice Objective Type Test (CBT). All candidates will be given a score based on their performance in the CBT. A final merit list will be prepared based on total marks obtained across all three sections. Selected candidates will go for document verification and medical examination. Appearance in the final merit list does not confer any right for appointment — a final offer letter will be issued only after successful completion of all pre-appointment formalities. BSNL reserves the right to cancel/restrict/enlarge/modify/alter the recruitment/selection process at any stage without notice.

Stage 1 – Computer Based Multiple Choice Objective Type Test (CBT)

Section Name of Test No. of Questions Maximum Marks Duration

II Engineering Stream Section – II 50 200
III General Ability Test Section – III 20 80
Total 120 480 3 Hours

Marking Scheme: For each correct answer: +4 Marks. For each wrong answer: -1 Mark (Negative Marking). The standard of engineering papers will be that of Engineering Degree Examination of an Indian University. In the General Ability Test, special attention will be paid to assess the candidate's capacity for general awareness, at the level expected of an Engineering Graduate. If the examination is held in multiple sessions, normalization of marks will be adopted. Minimum Qualifying Marks: For UR/OBC (CL) candidates — minimum 40% in each section and minimum 50% overall across all three sections combined. For SC/ST/OBC (NCL)/PwBD/EWS candidates — minimum 35% in each section and minimum 45% overall. Candidates not meeting sectional or overall minimum qualifying marks will not be included in the merit list. The final merit list will be prepared based on total marks in all three sections combined, subject to minimum qualifying marks criteria being met.

Stage 2 – Document Verification

Candidates in the declared merit list will be called for document verification. Date and venue will be intimated in due course. All original certificates along with self-attested photocopies must be produced at the time of document verification.

Stage 3 – Medical Examination

Appointment of selected candidates will be subject to their passing the Company's Medical Examination as per standards laid down by BSNL. Candidates who are already employed elsewhere must resign from their current organization only after being declared medically fit. Details will be provided on BSNL website www.bsnl.co.in.

BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026 - Exam Pattern & Syllabus

The examination is a Computer Based Multiple Choice Objective Type Test (CBT) of 3 hours duration consisting of three sections. Sections I and II cover Engineering Stream subjects at B.E./B.Tech. degree level, and Section III covers General Ability. The detailed syllabus topic-wise is given below.

Section I – Engineering Stream (Topics)

Topic Key Subtopics
1. Materials and Components Structure and properties of Electronic Engineering materials; Conductors, Semiconductors and Insulators; Magnetic, Ferroelectric, Piezoelectric, Ceramic, Optical and Superconducting materials; Passive components and characteristics – Resistors, Capacitors, Inductors; Ferrites, Quartz crystal, Ceramic resonators; Electromagnetic and Electromechanical components.
2. Physical Electronics, Electron Devices and ICs Electrons and holes in semiconductors; Carrier Statistics; Mechanics of current flow in a semi-conductor; Hall effect; Junction theory; Different types of diodes and their characteristics; Bipolar Junction transistor; Field effect transistors; Power switching devices like SCRs, CTOs, power MOSFETs; Basics of ICs-bipolar, MOS and CMOS types; Basics of Opto Electronics.
3. Network Theory Network analysis techniques; Network theorem; Transient and steady state sinusoidal response; Transmission criteria – delay and rise time, Elmore's and other definitions; Effect of cascading; Elements of network synthesis.
4. Electromagnetic Theory Transmission lines – basic theory, standing waves, matching applications, microstrip lines; Basics of waveguides and resonators; Elements of antenna theory.
5. Electronic Measurements and Instrumentation Basic concepts, standards and error analysis; Measurements of basic electrical quantities and parameters; Electronic measuring instruments and their principles of working – analog and digital, comparison, characteristics, applications; Transducers; Electronic measurements of non-electrical quantities like temperature, pressure, humidity; Basics of telemetry for industrial use.
6. Power Electronics Power Semiconductor devices; Thyristor; Power transistor; MOSFETs; Characteristics and operation; AC to DC convertors; 1-Phase and 3-phase DC to DC Convertors; AC regulators; Thyristor controlled reactors; Switched capacitor networks; Inverters – Single-phase and 3-phase; Pulse width modulation; Sinusoidal modulation with uniform sampling; Switched mode power supplies.

Section II – Engineering Stream (Topics)

Topic Key Subtopics
1. Analog Electronic Circuits Transistor biasing and stabilization; Small Signal analysis; Power amplifiers; Frequency response; Wide band techniques; Feedback amplifiers; Tuned amplifiers; Oscillators; Rectifiers and power supplies; Operational Amplifier; Other linear integrated circuits and applications; Pulse shaping circuits and waveform generators.
2. Digital Electronic Circuits Transistor as a switching element; Boolean algebra; Simplification of Boolean functions; Karnaugh Map and applications; IC Logic gates and their characteristics; IC logic families – DTL, TTL, ECL, NMOS, PMOS and CMOS gates and their comparison; Combinational logic circuits; Half adder, full adder; Digital Compartor; Multiplexer; Demultiplexer; ROM and their applications; Flip-flops – R-S, J-K, D and T types; Different types of counters and registers; Waveform generators; A/D and D/A converters; Semiconductor memories.
3. Control Systems Transient and steady state response of control systems; Effect of feedback on stability and sensitivity; Root locus techniques; Frequency response analysis; Concepts of gain and phase margins; Constant-M and Constant-N Nichol's Chart; Approximation of transient response from Constant-N Nichol's Chart; Approximation of transient response from closed loop frequency response; Design of Control Systems; Compensators; Industrial controllers.
4. Communication Systems Basic information theory; Modulation and detection in analogue and digital systems; Sampling and data reconstruction; Quantization & Coding; Time division and frequency division multiplexing; Equalisation; Optical Communication – in free space & fibre optic; Propagation of signals at HF, VHF, UHF and microwave frequency; Satellite communication.
5. Microwave Engineering Microwave Tubes and solid state devices; Microwave generation and amplifiers; Waveguides and other Microwave Components and Circuits; Microstrip circuits; Microwave antennas; Microwave Measurements; MASERS; LASERS; Microwave Propagation; Microwave Communication Systems – terrestrial and satellite based.
6. Computer Engineering Number Systems; Data representation; Programming; Elements of a high level programming language PASCAL/C; Use of basic data structures; Fundamentals of computer architecture processor design; Control unit design; Memory organization; I/O System Organization; Personal computers and their typical uses.
7. Microprocessors Microprocessor architecture – Instruction set and simple assembly language programming; Interfacing for memory and I/O; Applications of Microprocessors in Telecommunications and power system.

Section III – General Ability Test

Topic Key Subtopics
General Ability Test General English comprehension and understanding; Current Events and General Knowledge; Everyday observation and experience in scientific aspects as may be expected of an educated person; Events and developments in Telecommunications; History of India; Geography. Questions will be of a nature that can be answered without special study by an educated person.

Examination Centre Cities (27 Cities – ANNEXURE-C)

The examination will be held in 27 cities/centres across India. Candidates must choose only one Examination City/Centre at the time of registration. The exam centre may be any of the 27 cities or a nearby city depending upon number of candidates. The 27 cities are: Port Blair, Vijayawada, Guwahati, Patna, Chennai, Raipur, Ahmedabad, Ambala, Shimla, Jammu, Ranchi, Bangalore, Thiruvananthapuram, Kolkata, Bhopal, Mumbai, Shillong, Dimapur, New Delhi, Bhubaneshwar, Chandigarh, Jaipur, Gangtok, Hyderabad, Lucknow, Meerut, Dehradun. No request for change of examination centre will be entertained after submission.

BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026 - Bond, Training & Probation

All selected candidates for JTO(T)-DR will execute a Bond of Rs. 6 (Six) Lakhs in the format specified by BSNL to serve BSNL for a period of at least FIVE YEARS from the date of appointment as Junior Telecom Officer. Period of probation is Two Years. All JTO(T)-DR candidates must successfully undergo training for such period as may be specified by BSNL. Training details: JTO Phase-I training: 10 weeks; Field Training: 4 weeks; JTO Phase-II training (Specialisation course): 6 weeks. During training, the Direct Recruit JTO will be entitled to stipend (training allowance) as decided by BSNL from time to time. Seniority on appointment in JTO(T) cadre will be determined on the basis of 60% weightage of marks obtained in the DR Examination and 40% weightage of marks obtained in pre-appointment Phase-I training. In case of equal marks, seniority will be determined by date of birth (older candidate will be senior).

Competition Level Analysis for BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026

The competition level for BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026 is expected to be very high, as only 100 posts are available across 21 Circles for an All-India open market recruitment targeting Engineering graduates in Electronics/Telecom/CS/IT and related disciplines. Karnataka (26 seats), Kerala (15 seats), and Maharashtra (16 seats) will attract the highest number of serious applicants since they have the most vacancies and are also home to a large pool of engineering graduates. Circles like Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tamilnadu, and Uttarakhand with only 1 seat each will be the most competitive on a per-seat basis, where even a fraction of a mark can decide selection.

The 480-mark, 3-hour CBT with sectional minimum qualifying marks makes it critical to maintain balance across all three sections — candidates who neglect the General Ability section or fail to meet the per-section cut-off (40%/35%) will be eliminated regardless of their total score. The Rs. 2,000 exam fee and the mandatory 5-year bond (Rs. 6 Lakhs) will filter out casual applicants, leaving mostly serious engineering graduates. The Circle preference system rewards candidates who opt for more circles, as it gives BSNL flexibility to allocate based on merit and availability.

Who should NOT apply for BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026?

  • Candidates who do not hold a B.E./B.Tech. in any of the 7 specified disciplines (Telecom, Electronics, Radio, Computer, Electrical, IT, Instrumentation) or M.Sc. (Electronics/Computer Science) from a recognized University.
  • Candidates who cannot distinguish principal colours or do not have binocular vision — this is a mandatory eligibility condition for the JTO(T) post.
  • Candidates above 30 years of age as on 03-07-2026 (for UR/EWS/OBC-CL category) who do not qualify for any applicable relaxation.
  • Candidates not willing to serve anywhere in India or be transferred to any BSNL Circle — the post carries a liability to be transferred anywhere in India in the interest of service.
  • Candidates not willing to execute the bond of Rs. 6 Lakhs to serve BSNL for at least 5 years from the date of appointment.
  • Candidates who have entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a living spouse, or who having a living spouse, have entered into marriage with any person — such candidates are not eligible for appointment.
  • Candidates from outside India (Non-Indian Nationals) — only Indian Nationals are eligible.
  • OBC (Creamy Layer) candidates who wish to apply under OBC NCL reservation — Creamy Layer OBC candidates must indicate category as UR.

Common mistakes / What to check before applying BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026?

  • Not selecting enough Circle preferences during registration — candidates are strongly advised to select all 21 Circles in order of preference to maximise the chance of being selected based on merit. Opting for fewer Circles restricts candidature to only those opted Circles.
  • Uploading photograph or signature outside the prescribed size/format: photo must be in JPG/JPEG format, 20kb–50kb with white background; signature must be in JPG/JPEG format, 10kb–20kb only.
  • Using an incorrect or inactive mobile number/email ID — OTP will be sent to the registered mobile number for completing the registration process; all further communications will be sent only to these contacts.
  • Submitting multiple applications — in case of multiple registrations, only the latest application number will be considered as final and older applications will be rejected.
  • Not retaining the BSNL Registration Slip and Admit Card printout — no documents including copy of Registration Slip are to be sent to BSNL unless specifically asked.
  • Attempting to change the Examination Centre or discipline after submission — no such requests will be entertained.
  • Candidates already employed in Government Departments/Public Sector Undertakings/Autonomous Bodies must produce a "No Objection Certificate" from their present employer at the time of document verification — failure to produce this will affect appointment.
  • Not noting the Rs. 400/- challenge fee per question/answer key for post-exam grievance submission — this fee is non-refundable and must be paid online.
  • Underestimating negative marking — for every wrong answer, 1 mark is deducted. Avoid guessing randomly; unattempted questions carry no penalty.
  • Not checking sectional cut-offs — candidates must meet the minimum qualifying marks in each individual section (40% for UR/OBC-CL, 35% for reserved categories) in addition to the overall minimum, or they will not be considered for the merit list regardless of total marks.

How to Apply for BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026

Candidates shall apply online only through the BSNL External Exam portal (www.externalexam.bsnl.co.in). No manual/paper application will be entertained. Candidates should keep the following ready before starting the registration process: valid mobile number and email ID for OTP, scanned photograph, signature, Class 10th certificate, Degree Certificate, Consolidated Mark Sheet, Photo ID proof, Category/Disability Certificate (if applicable).

Documents Required to be Scanned and Uploaded:

  • Recent passport-size colour photograph with white background in JPG/JPEG format (20kb – 50kb only)
  • Signature in JPG/JPEG format (10kb – 20kb only)
  • Class 10th Certificate (for verification of Date of Birth)
  • Degree Certificate of Essential Qualification
  • Consolidated Mark Sheet / transcript of essential qualification for all semesters or years
  • Photo identity proof (Aadhaar Card, Passport, Driving License, Voter ID Card)
  • Valid proof of reservation category as applicable (SC/ST/OBC (NCL)/EWS/PwBD)
  • Medical Certificate for PwBD (issued by Govt. Medical Board in prescribed format)

Documents to be Produced at Document Verification / Appointment:

  • Admit Card (downloaded from www.externalexam.bsnl.co.in using username & password) along with valid photo identity proof in original
  • All original educational qualification certificates and mark sheets
  • Caste Certificate in prescribed Central Government format (for SC/ST candidates)
  • OBC (NCL) Certificate issued on or after 01.04.2026 in prescribed Central Government format (for OBC NCL candidates)
  • Income and Asset Certificate issued on or after 01.04.2026 in prescribed format (for EWS candidates)
  • Disability Certificate issued by Govt. Medical Board in prescribed format (for PwBD candidates)
  • "No Objection Certificate" from present employer (for candidates employed in Govt./PSU/Autonomous Bodies)
  • Date of Birth proof (Matriculation / Secondary School Leaving Certificate or equivalent)

Apply Online at: https://www.externalexam.bsnl.co.in

For queries: Contact BSNL Corporate Office, New Delhi at [email protected]. BSNL does not seek payments of any kind other than the registration fee and post-exam grievance fee. Candidates are advised not to respond to unscrupulous advertisements; check authenticity only on www.bsnl.co.in.

Important Instructions for BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026 Candidates

  • Both internal BSNL employees and external (open market) candidates fulfilling the prescribed eligibility conditions are eligible to apply.
  • JTO is a Circle Cadre post; candidates will be allotted a Circle depending on vacancies, their preference, and merit. Options once exercised shall be final — change of Circle afterwards will not be allowed.
  • Candidates are strongly advised to select all 21 Circles in order of preference to maximise the possibility of selection. Selecting a limited number of Circles restricts candidature only to those opted Circles.
  • All selected candidates must execute a Bond of Rs. 6 Lakhs to serve BSNL for at least 5 years from the date of appointment as Junior Telecom Officer.
  • The admit card will be available only for download from the BSNL website — it will NOT be sent by post or email. Issuance of admit card does not confer any right for appointment.
  • After closing of registration period, an Editing Window will be opened for 7 days — candidates can edit selective fields only. No further editing will be allowed after the editing period.
  • Candidates applying for UR vacancy can also be SC/ST/EWS/OBC/Ex-Serviceman/BSNL employees subject to meeting all general eligibility standards — category relaxation in such cases cannot be availed.
  • Candidature is liable to be rejected at any stage if any information provided is found false or not in conformity with the eligibility criteria mentioned in the advertisement.
  • No request for withdrawal of candidature will be entertained. Any dispute will be subject to the courts/tribunals having jurisdiction at New Delhi.
  • Canvassing in any form or influencing officials related to the selection/recruitment process will result in immediate disqualification of the candidate.
  • Candidates who have a living spouse and have entered into another marriage, or who have married a person with a living spouse, are not eligible for appointment.
  • BSNL reserves the right to modify/amend any terms and conditions of this recruitment at any point of time. Dispute, if any, shall be within the jurisdiction of Delhi only.
  • BSNL Management reserves the right to cancel the recruitment exercise fully/partially at any stage at its discretion without notice.
  • BSNL does not seek payments of any kind other than the registration fee and post-exam grievance fee — candidates are advised to beware of fraudulent advertisements.

C-DAC JIT June 2026 Recruitment – Selection Process

Selection is multi-stage: initial academic screening, followed by a written test if required, and a personal interview. Only shortlisted candidates are contacted by email - no hard copy communication is sent at any stage.

Stage 1 – Initial Screening

All applications are screened based on academic records, qualifications, experience, and other parameters declared in the online application. Only candidates who meet the minimum eligibility criteria are screened in for further selection. C-DAC reserves the right to raise the minimum cut-off if the number of applicants is significantly higher than vacancies.

Stage 2 – Written Test (if applicable)

Depending on the number of screened-in applicants and centre requirements, a written/skill test may be conducted. This is at the discretion of the respective C-DAC centre. Candidates will be informed through email only. No TA/DA is paid for attending the written test.

Stage 3 – Personal Interview

Shortlisted candidates are called for a personal interview by the respective C-DAC centre. The interview call letter will be sent via email only. Mere receipt of an interview call letter does not confirm selection or acceptance of candidature. No TA/DA is paid for attending the interview.

Competition Level Analysis for C-DAC JIT June 2026 Recruitment

The C-DAC JIT June 2026 Recruitment is a large-scale opportunity with openings across 11 centres and hundreds of positions spanning fresher to senior levels. Competition is expected to be moderate to high for roles in high-demand domains such as AI/ML, Full Stack Development, Cyber Security, and Software Development, particularly at the Project Engineer and Senior Project Engineer levels, which attract the largest pools of applicants from tier-2 and tier-3 engineering colleges. Vacancies for niche domains like Quantum Computing, VLSI, Additive Manufacturing, Robotics, and HPC System Software will see comparatively lower competition but require highly specialised credentials. The absence of any application fee significantly increases the applicant volume.

Effective competition will be filtered through the initial academic screening stage, where CGPA, percentage, and domain relevance determine shortlisting. Candidates who have internships, publications, or project work in their declared domain may gain an advantage even if such experience is not counted formally. For experienced positions, those with documented employer-issued experience certificates closely matching the domain will clear the first cut. Candidates applying to Noida (e-Governance, Health Informatics) and Pune (high volume, 200+ positions) will face steeper competition due to location preference and breadth of domain coverage.

Who Should NOT Apply for C-DAC JIT June 2026 Recruitment?

  • Candidates looking for a permanent government job - all positions are purely contractual with no guarantee of regular appointment in C-DAC.
  • Candidates whose qualification is from a college/university NOT approved by AICTE/UGC or not recognized by the Central/State Government - their candidature will be rejected.
  • Candidates unable to produce CGPA-to-percentage conversion proof from their university if their institution uses a CGPA/letter grade system.
  • Candidates who want to count internship, project placements, teaching, or research work as experience - these are explicitly excluded unless the specific post mentions otherwise.
  • Candidates without valid experience certificates from past/present employers clearly showing period of employment, salary, and designation - experience without documentary proof will not be considered.
  • C-DAC internal candidates who have not completed at least 2 years of service in C-DAC as on 20 June 2026.
  • Candidates unwilling to be deputed or transferred to any C-DAC project location across India - selected candidates may be posted anywhere in India as per organizational requirement.
  • Candidates who are not comfortable with purely email-based communication - all call letters, interview invitations, and correspondence are sent by email only; no hard copies are sent.
  • Candidates whose age exceeds the upper age limit for the applied post as on 20 June 2026, and who do not possess valid category certificates for applicable relaxations.
  • Candidates seeking to canvass or influence the selection process - canvassing in any form is a disqualification.

Common Mistakes / What to Check Before Applying for C-DAC JIT June 2026 Recruitment?

  • Applying to the wrong centre - each centre has a separate advertisement and separate application link; applying on one centre's form does not cover other centres.
  • Not submitting a separate application for each post - candidates applying for multiple positions must submit individual applications for each one.
  • Uploading a resume in the wrong format - only PDF format (max 500 KB) is accepted; photographs must be in .jpg format (max 400 KB).
  • Not noting the unique application number generated after submission - this is needed for future reference and tracking.
  • Government/PSU/Autonomous body employees forgetting to forward their signed application through proper channel to the respective HRD section - those not doing so must produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their current employer at the time of interview.
  • Claiming experience from internships, academic projects, or teaching without checking whether the specific post allows it - most posts do not count such work as experience.
  • Sending hard copies of applications, mark sheets, or resumes to C-DAC - no documents should be sent physically; all applications are online only.
  • Assuming the interview call letter confirms selection - it does not; candidature is subject to document verification at any stage.
  • Internal C-DAC candidates forgetting that if finally selected, they must resign from their current C-DAC service and join as a fresh employee for the selected post.
  • Not visiting the official C-DAC website regularly - all corrigenda, extensions, and updates are published only on www.cdac.in and no other platform.

How to Apply for C-DAC JIT June 2026 Recruitment

Candidates must apply online only through the C-DAC careers portal (https://careers.cdac.in/). No offline/hard copy applications are accepted. A valid mobile number and email ID are mandatory as OTP-based login is used and all communications are sent by email only.

Documents Required to be Scanned and Uploaded:

  • Passport-size photograph in .jpg format (not more than 400 KB)
  • Resume / CV in PDF format (not more than 500 KB)

Documents to be Produced at the time of Document Verification / Joining:

  • All educational mark sheets and degree certificates from Class 10 onwards
  • CGPA-to-percentage conversion certificate issued by the university (if applicable)
  • Experience certificates from all previous and current employers clearly indicating period of employment, salary drawn, and post held
  • Caste/category certificate in prescribed Government of India format (SC/ST/OBC Non-Creamy Layer/EWS) where applicable
  • Disability certificate in prescribed format issued by the District Medical Board (for PwBD candidates)
  • SSLC/SSC/ISC mark sheet or other valid document as proof of date of birth
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) from current employer (if not forwarded through proper channel)
  • Any other document evidencing eligibility as declared in the application

Apply Online at: https://careers.cdac.in/ → Select the relevant centre → Click 'Apply' against the desired position → Log in with mobile number → Enter OTP → Fill and submit application form.

Important Instructions for C-DAC JIT June 2026 Recruitment Candidates

  • These are CONTRACTUAL positions - no right to regular or permanent employment in C-DAC is created by engagement under this recruitment.
  • Candidates may be deputed or transferred from one project to another at any C-DAC project location across India based on organizational requirement.
  • The contract is initially for up to 3 years (1 year for Kolkata centre) or project completion, whichever is earlier. Extension is possible based on performance and project requirement.
  • All correspondence including interview call letters will be sent by email only - candidates must keep their registered email ID and mobile number active throughout the process.
  • C-DAC reserves the right to increase/decrease the number of posts, change eligibility criteria, cancel any or all positions, or modify/cancel the selection process at any stage without notice.
  • If selected candidates are found ineligible at any stage - even after joining - their engagement is liable to be terminated without notice.
  • No TA/DA is payable for attending the written test or interview at any centre.
  • C-DAC has not authorized any agent or agency to represent it for recruitment matters - beware of fraudulent offers.
  • All updates, corrigenda, and extensions will be published only on the official website www.cdac.in.
  • Canvassing in any form will result in disqualification.

Experience Post-qualification experience only (experience counted only after passing the essential qualification). Scientist E: 11 years; Scientist D: 7 years; Scientist C: 3 years (as on closing date). Experience below Pay Level 10 as per 7th CPC or equivalent will not be considered.
CCA Declaration / NOC All serving candidates in Government/PSU/Government-promoted companies (with 50% or more controlling stake) must upload a signed CCA Declaration at time of online submission. NOC from Cadre Controlling Authority (CCA) is mandatory at time of Final Personal Interview.

(Only if in the relevant discipline and acquired before closing date; period of study must not overlap with work experience.)

DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Screening of received applications will be carried out at multiple stages. Final selection is purely based on merit of marks scored in the Final Personal Interview.

Stage 1 – Administrative Screening: Verification of identity, age, essential & higher qualifications, length of suitable experience and CCA Declaration (wherever applicable).

Stage 2 – Technical Screening (Level-1): For all Administratively Eligible candidates - Technical Screening by holding a Meeting of Technical Screening Committee (an independent body including Technical Experts from Industry/Academia/DRDO other than RAC) using Bio-data based Technical Screening at Level-1 by: (a) Relevance of suitable experience w.r.t. advertised qualifications; (b) Relevance of Desirable/Higher Qualification; (c) Any other criteria suggested by Technical Screening Committee. Predefined Ratio for Preliminary Online Interview: Up to 24 candidates for 1 post; up to 48 candidates for 2 posts.

Stage 3 – Technical Screening (Level-2 / Preliminary Online Interview, if required): If number shortlisted for Final Personal Interview is large, further shortlisting via Preliminary Online Interview of short duration (10–15 minutes). Predefined Ratio for Final Personal Interview: Up to 12 candidates for 1 post; up to 24 candidates for 2 posts.

Stage 4 – Final Personal Interview (in-person at RAC, Delhi): Final selection is purely on merit of marks scored. Candidates must score a minimum of 75% marks (75 out of 100) in the Final Personal Interview for consideration for selection. The Final Personal Interview will be held in-person only before the Selection Board at RAC, Delhi on the scheduled date - no online/virtual interview will be considered.

Note: If administrative screening does not result in minimum 6 eligible candidates against one vacancy, the subsequent selection process for that vacancy may be cancelled. If technical screening does not result in minimum 6 candidates per vacancy for Final Personal Interview, the number of vacancies will be reduced accordingly.

Competition Level Analysis for DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026

The competition level for DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026 is expected to be very high, particularly for Scientist C posts in Electronics & Communication Engineering, Computer Science & Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering - disciplines with a large pool of eligible candidates and growing interest in DRDO's prestigious research environment. DRDO provides one of the best career growth structures for scientists under the Flexible Complimenting Scheme (FCS), making it a highly sought-after employer.

The multi-stage shortlisting process (Administrative → Technical Level-1 → Level-2/Preliminary Online Interview → Final Personal Interview in Delhi) is rigorous. Only up to 12 candidates per vacancy reach the Final Personal Interview, and even among those, a minimum of 75% marks in the interview is mandatory for selection. For Scientist D and E posts requiring 7–11 years of experience, the competition narrows to experienced professionals, but the specificity of required experience (e.g., Optics/Photonics, Radiation Physics, Chemical Engineering for underwater applications) naturally limits the eligible pool, making those posts relatively less competitive. Niche posts like Oceanography, Pharmacology, and Remote Sensing will see very limited candidates, improving selection chances for well-qualified applicants.

Who should NOT apply for DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026?

  • Candidates who do not have First Division (60%+) in the essential qualifying degree - this is a hard minimum requirement and no rounding off is permitted.
  • Candidates with experience below Pay Level 10 (7th CPC) or equivalent - such experience will not be counted for computing the required years of experience.
  • Candidates whose period of study (higher qualification like PhD) overlaps with the work experience claimed - overlapping periods will be removed from total experience.
  • Candidates applying for Scientist D or E posts who are currently unemployed for more than one year - under current employment, the period of un-employment shall not exceed one year, else the candidature will be rejected.
  • Candidates serving in Government/PSU who do not upload a signed CCA Declaration - without CCA Declaration their candidature will be rejected, and NOC will be mandatory at Final Personal Interview.
  • Candidates from Private Sector who cannot produce CTC/Pay drawn proof/Form 16A for the claimed experience period - this is the sole criteria for establishing experience suitability from private sector.
  • Candidates exceeding the maximum age of 35 years (Scientist C), 45 years (Scientist D/E), or 56 years inclusive of all relaxations.
  • Candidates who cannot attend the Final Personal Interview in-person at RAC, Delhi - no online/virtual mode is available for Final Personal Interview under any circumstances.
  • Candidates who do not meet the specific work experience fields mentioned in the advertised qualifications - the Technical Screening Committee assesses relevance of experience very strictly.
  • Candidates applying for Scientist C (Encadered) posts from Reserved categories seeking age relaxation - there is no category-based age relaxation for Scientist C Encadered posts.

Common mistakes / What to check before applying for DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026?

  • Not checking whether your experience is at or above Pay Level 10 (7th CPC) equivalent - experience below this level is invalid and will not be counted.
  • Miscounting experience years by including the period of higher qualification (PhD/M.Tech) that overlaps with work experience - the overlapping period will be deducted.
  • Applying for multiple posts by submitting one application - candidates applying for more than one post must apply separately for each post and mention item numbers of all other posts where they have applied, along with the order of preference.
  • Not highlighting desirable qualifications and experience in the Justification column under 'Other Section' in the online application form - this is crucial for Technical Screening Committee's assessment.

Key Highlights

  • Advertisement No.: 03/2026, issued by Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board (DSSSB) dated 29/05/2026.
  • Total Vacancies: 1,979 posts across 25 post codes in multiple departments of Government of NCT of Delhi.
  • Departments: Forensic Science Laboratory, Directorate of Education, New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC), Information Technology Department, Department of Delhi Archives, and Labour Department.

  • Qualification: Ranges from Matric/ITI (for technical posts) to Master's degree (for scientific/teaching posts) depending on the post.
  • Age Limit: Varies by post - generally 18–27 years for scientific posts, up to 30–32 years for technical/teaching posts. Age relaxation applicable as per Central Government rules.
  • Exam Type: One Tier (General) or One Tier (Technical/Teaching) Computer Based Test of 200 marks. Negative marking of 0.25 marks per wrong answer.

The Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board (DSSSB) has released Advertisement No. 03/2026, inviting online applications from eligible candidates for recruitment to 1,979 posts across 25 different post codes in various departments and autonomous bodies of the Government of NCT of Delhi. This is one of the largest DSSSB recruitment cycles in 2026, covering a wide range of profiles - from Junior Scientific Assistants in the Forensic Science Laboratory to Trained Graduate Teachers (Computer Science) in the Directorate of Education, and technical posts such as Fitter, Lift Operator, Sub Station Apprentice, and Electrical Overseer in NDMC and the Labour Department. The notification was issued on 29 May 2026 and the online application window opens on 16 June 2026.

All posts are permanent government positions under the Government of NCT of Delhi or its autonomous and local bodies. Candidates can apply online only through the DSSSB portal at dsssbonline.nic.in. The closing date for all applications is 15 July 2026. Eligibility criteria - including age, educational qualification, and experience - will be determined as on the closing date of application, i.e., 15 July 2026.

DSSSB 03/2026 - Post-wise Eligibility, Qualification & Pay Scale

Eligibility requirements differ significantly across the 25 post codes in this advertisement. For all 11 Junior Scientific Assistant posts in the Forensic Science Laboratory (post codes 21/26 to 31/26), the minimum educational qualification is a Master's degree in the relevant science subject from a recognized university, and the age limit is 18 to 27 years with a pay scale of ₹29,200 – ₹92,300 (Pay Level 5). For teaching posts in the Directorate of Education (post codes 41/26 to 44/26), graduation with B.Ed or a relevant Diploma in Special Education is required along with CTET qualification wherever applicable, and the pay scale ranges from ₹35,400 – ₹1,12,400 to ₹44,900 – ₹1,42,400 depending on the post group. For technical posts in NDMC and the Labour Department, ITI certificates or Diplomas in the relevant trade are required. The IT Assistant Grade-A post (34/26) requires only a Class 12 pass with a typing speed of 8,000 key depressions per hour. All newly recruited candidates must undergo a mandatory induction training of at least two weeks as a prerequisite for probation completion.

DSSSB 03/2026 - Age Limit & Age Relaxation

Age limits for posts in DSSSB Advertisement 03/2026 vary by post. Most Junior Scientific Assistant posts (FSL) have an age limit of 18 to 27 years. Teaching posts in the Directorate of Education have an upper age limit of 30 years. Technical posts in NDMC vary between 18–32 years and 18–37 years depending on the post. The eligibility for age will be determined as on the closing date of application, 15 July 2026. Age relaxation is available for SC/ST (5 years), OBC-Delhi (3 years), PwBD (10 years), Ex-Servicemen (military service period plus 3 years), and departmental candidates (up to 40 years for Group C posts in the same line). Contractual employees of the same department may also claim one-time age relaxation up to 5 years, subject to having worked at least 180 working days (or 120 days for teaching posts) in that particular year.

Fee once paid will not be refunded under any circumstances. Payment must be made through SBI e-Pay only. No other mode of payment will be accepted.

DSSSB 03/2026 Examination Scheme & Selection Process

Selection for all posts in DSSSB Advertisement 03/2026 will be through a Computer Based Test (CBT). The exam scheme is divided into three types depending on the post. Post codes 34/26, 39/26, and 40/26 (IT Assistant Grade-A, Data Processing Assistant, Data Entry Operator) will be examined under the One Tier General (I-T-G) scheme - a 2-hour paper of 200 MCQs covering General Awareness, Reasoning, Numerical Ability, Hindi, and English (40 marks each). All Forensic Science Laboratory posts, NDMC technical posts, Delhi Archives posts, and the Electrical Overseer post (i.e., post codes 21/26 to 33/26, 35/26 to 38/26, and 45/26) will follow the One Tier Technical (I-T-T) scheme - a 2-hour paper split into Section A (100 MCQs on general subjects, 100 marks) and Section B (100 MCQs on the domain subject, 100 marks). Teaching posts - TGT Computer Science, Domestic Science Teacher, TGT Special Education, and Special Educator Primary (post codes 41/26 to 44/26) - follow the One Tier Technical/Teaching scheme with the same structure, where Section B includes questions on teaching methodology and B.Ed syllabus.

Negative marking of 0.25 marks applies for every wrong MCQ answer. Questions will be bilingual (Hindi and English), except language-specific papers. The minimum qualifying marks are 40% for General/EWS, 35% for OBC (Delhi), and 30% for SC/ST/PwBD. Ex-Servicemen get an additional 5% relaxation in their respective categories, subject to a minimum of 30%.

How to Apply for DSSSB Recruitment 2026 (Advertisement No. 03/2026)

Candidates must apply online only through the official DSSSB portal at dsssbonline.nic.in. Before applying, candidates must complete a one-time registration on the portal. The same user ID and password can be used for all future DSSSB examinations - no separate registration is required for each post. However, only one online application is allowed per post code; if multiple applications are detected for the same post code, all will be rejected and the candidate may be debarred. Once an application is submitted, no corrections or modifications - including change of category - will be permitted under any circumstances.

Candidates are advised to apply well before the closing date of 15 July 2026 to avoid last-minute technical issues. The application fee of ₹100 must be paid through SBI e-Pay; no other payment mode is accepted. After successful submission, candidates should download and save a printout of their application for future reference. All supporting documents (educational certificates, caste certificates, experience certificates, etc.) will be required at the time of e-dossier upload, which will be called separately after the written examination. Candidates who fail to upload their e-dossier within the given time will have their candidature cancelled with no further opportunity.

  • Visit the DSSSB portal: https://dsssbonline.nic.in
  • Complete one-time registration (if not already registered).
  • Login and select the relevant post code from Advertisement No. 03/2026.
  • Fill in all details carefully - no changes can be made after submission.
  • Pay the application fee of ₹100 via SBI e-Pay (exempted for Women/SC/ST/PwBD/ESM).
  • Upload a recent colour passport photo (plain white/off-white background, clear face, eyes open) and signature.
  • Submit and download the application form printout.
  • Exam date will be announced separately on the DSSSB website.

DSSSB 03/2026 - Reservation & OBC Certificate Rules

Reservation benefits are available for SC, ST, OBC (Delhi), EWS, PwBD, ESM, and Meritorious Sports Persons as per Government of NCT of Delhi and Central Government instructions. An important point for OBC candidates: only OBC (Delhi) candidates notified by the Government of NCT of Delhi are eligible for reservation. OBC candidates from outside Delhi will be treated as Unreserved (UR) candidates and must apply under the UR category.

OBC (Delhi) candidates must possess a valid OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate issued on or after 01/04/2026 but not later than 15/07/2026 (the closing date). For EWS candidates, an Income & Asset certificate valid for financial year 2026–27, based on income of financial year 2025–26, is required. The reservation roster, earmarking of vacancies, and PwBD post suitability are determined entirely by the respective User Departments, not by DSSSB.

DSSSB 03/2026 - Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Only one registration is allowed per candidate on the DSSSB portal. Multiple registrations will lead to cancellation of all applications.
  • Only one application per post code is allowed. Multiple applications for the same post code will result in cancellation and debarment.
  • The eligibility cut-off date is 15 July 2026 - age, qualification, experience, and all other eligibility conditions will be determined as on this date.
  • DSSSB does not verify eligibility at the application stage; candidature is accepted on a provisional basis. Verification happens at the e-dossier stage after the written examination.
  • No calculator, mobile phone, Bluetooth device, earbud, camera, smartwatch, or any other electronic gadget is allowed in the examination hall.
  • Dress code: light clothes with half sleeves, no big buttons, brooch, or badge; salwar/trouser; slippers or sandals with low heels. Shoes are not allowed.
  • Exam centres will be in Delhi/NCR and other states as decided by DSSSB.
  • DSSSB reserves the right to cancel, modify, or amend any part of the advertisement or examination at any stage.
  • In case of any discrepancy between the English, Hindi, Urdu, and Punjabi versions of the advertisement, the English version will be treated as final.
  • Candidates must regularly check the DSSSB website at https://dsssb.delhi.gov.in for updates and notifications/corrigenda.

In summary, DSSSB Advertisement No. 03/2026 offers 1,979 government job vacancies across 25 post codes in Delhi. The largest vacancy categories are TGT Computer Science (675 posts) in the Directorate of Education, Special Educator Primary (450 posts), JSA Cyber Forensic (81 posts) in the Forensic Science Laboratory, and IT Assistant Grade-A (125 posts) in the Information Technology Department. Candidates from a wide range of educational backgrounds - Class 12 pass to Master's degree holders - can find suitable posts in this advertisement. The application window is open from 16 June 2026 to 15 July 2026 and all candidates must apply online at dsssbonline.nic.in. The written examination, which will be a Computer Based Test, will be scheduled and notified separately on the DSSSB website at dsssb.delhi.gov.in.

RRB ALP Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must fulfill all eligibility conditions as on the closing date of online application (14-06-2026). Educational/Technical qualification certificates must be from a recognized Board/University/Institute. Candidates awaiting results of their final examination for the prescribed qualification are NOT eligible to apply. The post of ALP is not suitable for Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD). Candidates who have undergone Lasik Surgery or any other corrective eye surgery are not eligible for this post.

Educational Qualification

Option Details
Option A - Matriculation + ITI Matriculation / SSLC plus ITI from recognised institutions of NCVT/SCVT in the trades of Fitter, Electrician, Instrument Mechanic, Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic, Mechanic (Radio & TV), Electronics Mechanic, Mechanic (Motor Vehicle), Wireman, Tractor Mechanic, Armature & Coil Winder, Mechanic (Diesel), Heat Engine, Turner, Machinist, Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic. RRB ALP Recruitment 2026 - Age Limit

Candidates must be between 18 and 30 years of age as on 01-07-2026. Age relaxation is available for various categories as detailed below. If a candidate is eligible for relaxation on more than one ground, only the maximum relaxation will be granted (not cumulative). SC, ST, and OBC (NCL) candidates applying against UR vacancies will not get any age relaxation. There is no fixed limit on the number of attempts - candidates can appear as long as they are within the prescribed upper age limit.

RRB ALP Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

Candidates are required to pay the non-refundable recruitment fee online. Fee can be paid only through online mode - internet banking, debit/credit cards, or UPI. Applications received without the prescribed fee will be summarily rejected. Candidates who appear in CBT-1 will receive a refund of their examination fee (after deducting applicable bank charges) credited to their Aadhaar-seeded bank account. Candidates whose applications are rejected, or who do not appear in CBT-1, will not receive any refund.
